rat noun

also squeak, like drowned rats

medieval

M-O s.v. rat
Andresian p. 25
Traupman 368

rattus, rattī m.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

Medieval (Morgan–Owens, who cites it from Pallas, 1811); not in Lewis & Short. Classical Latin had no separate word for the rat.

Other words

  • mūs, mūris m. — mouse; any mouse or rat

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Plin. NH 8.57.82 (chapter numbering; Lewis & Short); Traupman 144 · Declension on Wiktionary

    The ancients took the rat and other small beasts under mūs (Lewis & Short); see mouse.

  • mintriō, mintrīre — squeak (of a mouse or rat)

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · late Latin · Auct. Carm. Philom. (Lewis & Short); Traupman 368 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

Examples

  • homō nēquam

    a rat (a worthless person)Traupman 368

  • tamquam mūrēs ūdī

    like drowned ratsTraupman 368

  • Rattī mintriunt.

    Rats squeak.Traupman 368

See also mouse.
